clock_dir_to: kém ("less") names the hour being APPROACHED and subtracts from it:
"ba giờ kém mười" is 02:50, ten to three.  Mirror image of rưỡi, which
counts forward from the hour it names; both idioms are in daily use and
neither direction can be made the locale's default.
clock_fraction_30: rưỡi is "and a half", counted from the hour ALREADY NAMED -- the English
"half past" direction, not the Germanic toward-the-hour one: the
dictionary's own worked example is "ba (giờ) rưỡi chiều" == 3:30 PM.  It
attaches with or without giờ, hence the optional hour word in the order.
The same locale's kém counts the OTHER way (see clock_dir_to.voc); the
direction is a property of the word here, not of the language.
clock_meridiem_night: đêm is the night BAND, 21:00 round to 04:00 -- it crosses midnight, so it
is not a flat twelve-hour shift: "một giờ đêm" is 01:00, not 13:00.
clock_meridiem_pm: chiều is the afternoon band (12:00-18:00), tối the evening one

marker_at: giờ marks the hour it follows ("hai giờ" == two o'clock); lúc points at
a definite time and precedes it ("lúc hai giờ").
marker_bc: trước Công Nguyên, "before the common era", listed among trước's derived
terms, with its usual abbreviation.  The bare "cn" is not admitted -- it
is also CLDR's abbreviation for Sunday.
marker_day_word: "ngày 5 tháng 3" -- the day noun introducing a day of the month.
marker_future: sau is "after, later", the antonym trước's own entry names, and trails
the duration the same way ("ba ngày sau").
marker_last: The before/after prepositions double as the last/next period markers,
postposed to the unit noun: "tuần trước" is last week.
marker_minute_word: The minute noun closing a spoken clock ("ba giờ kém mười lăm phút").
marker_next: "tuần sau" is next week; sau's own entry glosses the adjective as
marker_ordinal_prefix: "thứ" prefixes a numeral to make it an ordinal ("thứ tám" eighth).  The same
word names a weekday when the numeral is one word long ("thứ hai" Monday),
which is why it is optional wherever an ordinal is already unambiguous:
"thế kỷ 20" and "thế kỷ thứ 20" are the same twentieth century.
marker_past: trước is "before" and "ago", trailing the duration it counts back over
("ba ngày trước").  cách đây is the dedicated "ago" adverb and PRECEDES
the duration ("cách đây ba ngày"); both orders are declared, so the
marker's side of the count is a property of the word, not of the locale.
marker_year_word: "năm 2024" -- the year noun introducing a Gregorian year.
month_1: Months are numbered too -- tháng ("month") plus the number -- and CLDR
gives no lexical month names at all, only "tháng 1".."tháng 12" wide
and "thg 1".. abbreviated.  The spelled numbering is the same
construction, and month four takes the positional substitute tư rather
Spelled forms and the lunar-calendar alternates giêng (January) and chạp

named_day_-2: hôm kia and ngày kia are a minimal pair pointing in OPPOSITE directions:
both close on kia, and only the head noun -- hôm for the past family,
ngày for the future one -- says which.  Matching on kia alone would put
with its own "not to be confused with ngày kia" note).
named_day_1: ngày mai, with the colloquial short form mai.
named_day_2: The future half of the hôm kia / ngày kia pair -- see named_day_-2.voc.
The southern ngày mốt is listed, but its bare short form mốt is not: on
its own mốt is the numeral one in a tens compound (hai mươi mốt == 21).
scope_unit_decade: See unit_decade.voc.  "thập niên" is the collective head of the
decade-naming phrase ("thập niên 80") and is listed alongside them.
season_summer: mùa hè and its synonym mùa hạ.
unit_century: Both spellings of the same Sino-Vietnamese compound.
unit_decade: Both spellings of the same Sino-Vietnamese compound.
unit_hour: giờ is both the hour as a duration and the word that marks a point on
the clock ("bốn giờ" == four o'clock), exactly as Turkish saat is.
unit_millennium: Both spellings of the same Sino-Vietnamese compound.
unit_year: năm is the noun "year" and, separately, the numeral five -- the same
spelling and the same tone.  The numeral fold never reads a bare năm
as five, so this reading is the only one it has.

ways -- wide "Thứ Hai", abbreviated "Thứ 2" -- and both are listed,
because they are one construction in two spellings, not a name and an
